A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 33-page versions of the same work, with matching main sections and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered pages support comparison of the equations, algorithms, and table.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical algorithms, sample-complexity guarantees, proofs, and constructed MDP counterexamples. Table 1 specifies Q-function values for a proof; it does not report experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical treatment and constructed examples. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The proposed algorithms and losses are unchanged. Equation (9) removes the redundant optimization variable R, but its objective already depended only on f, and Algorithm 2 already specified optimization solely over f.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or tasks actually used in empirical training or evaluation. The theoretical MDP settings and constructed examples are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations. The analytical comparisons with GOLF in Section 5 and Appendix F.1 are unchanged.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocol appears in either version. The algorithmic sampling procedures and theoretical parameter prescriptions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 retains the same analytical failure example for separately fitting rewards and value functions. Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Their theoretical concentration bounds and high-probability guarantees are unchanged.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. Table 1's constructed numerical values and the stated sample-complexity guarantees remain unchanged; the changed proof identity is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2, page 33, changes E[(1-R2)/3 | pi^theta] = <theta,v>/3 to E[1/3-R2 | pi^theta] = <theta,v>/3. This corrects the affine reward transformation in the linear-bandit reduction. The theorem statements, assumptions, and complexity bounds are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about coverability-based guarantees, deterministic-MDP simplification, preference feedback, and exponential separation between outcome and process feedback.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning joint optimization, failure of separate reward fitting, computational limitations, deterministic-MDP advantages, and the boundaries of outcome feedback remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm descriptions and theoretical parameter choices are retained. Neither version adds implementation instructions, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code and data access information.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Antos et al. (2008) to the attribution for addressing double sampling through the Bellman-loss correction. This work already appeared in Appendix A and the bibliography, so the change is a limited attribution refinement.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgements section after the conclusion, updates the document date, and makes isolated citation and equation edits. The narrative and substantive section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements shift the References section and reflow bibliography entries across pages 10–13. Equation edits also produce small local layout changes. Table 1 and the algorithm boxes are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected reward transformation in Appendix F.2 resolves a false equality in the process-feedback reduction. Removing the redundant variable in Equation (9) also improves consistency with Algorithm 2. These provide limited gains in mathematical accuracy and clarity while leaving the substantive results unchanged.
